maria (AE): quick sync — RetailCo wants to run a 4-week trial to validate two things: 1) relevance for on-site search + autocomplete, 2) product description generation for catalog pages. can we sketch use cases and success criteria?
aj (SE): +1. main constraints they flagged: latency requirement for autocomplete (~<100ms p95), data residency EU-only, and ability to fall back to a cheaper model for bulk batch generation.
maria (AE): pricing question — they asked about per-token vs reserved capacity for a pilot (expected 50k queries/day, ~200 tokens/query for gen). what do we recommend?
kevin (sales_eng): for that volume reserved dedicated is overkill for a pilot. suggest hosted API with higher rate limits + burst for autocomplete. show them cost estimates and a Dedicated option if they commit to 6-12 months.
jules (solutions): proposed POC plan (4 weeks):
- week 0: infra & security questionnaire + API keys + EU region setup
- week 1: integrate autocomplete endpoint + realtime latency baseline
- week 2: product description generation + eval harness (prompt sets)
- week 3: tuning (batching, quantization recs) + canary rollouts between model variants
- week 4: final eval, cost analysis, recommendation + signoff
tom (CS): add success criteria:
- Autocomplete: R95 latency < 150ms (client-to-response), relevance NDCG@5 > 0.6 vs baseline
- Product desc: 85% pass rate on semantic quality checks (no hallucinations, SKU accuracy) on 200-sample eval set
- Ops: error rate < 0.5% and fallback configured to smaller model for cost-saving bursts
maria (AE): re: security — they sent an initial vendor questionnaire. items flagged: SOC2, KMS integration, network peering options, and audit logs. can eng confirm which are ready?
aj (SE): SOC2 + basic KMS integrations supported. VPC peering we can do via Private deployment but needs 2–3 weeks + infra engagement. audit logs available via Console (retention limits depend on plan).
kevin (sales_eng): let's be explicit in the POC scope: must include EU-resident hosted environment (we can spin up in eu-central), no customer data sent to non-EU regions, and all keys managed via their KMS if they choose. If VPC-required then timeline extends.
maria (AE): great — can someone draft the minimal deliverables doc for their legal + security team? short one-pager.
jules (solutions): I’ll draft. will include: endpoints, sample prompts, data flow diagram, SLA for pilot, and estimated cost buckets.
aj (SE): sample endpoints to include in doc (feel free to copy):
```
POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate (region: eu-central)
body: {"model": "redwood-mini-1.1", "prompt": "<user_query>", "max_tokens": 256, "stream": false}

POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/autocomplete
body: {"model": "redwood-fast-embed", "prefix": "<partial_input>", "limit": 6}
```
maria (AE): nice. add the eval prompt set example for product desc so we can share with their PM.
jules (solutions): sample eval prompts (200 items total):
- "Write a 50-word description for SKU: 12345 — include material and color."
- "Summarize key care instructions for SKU: 67890."
- "List top-3 compatible accessories for SKU: 24680."
Expectations: perfect match on SKU attributes, no invented specs; score pass/fail and free-text quality rating 1–5.
tom (CS): also include monitoring hooks: trace id in responses, token-level cost logging, and dashboard link for per-route latency. will help them evaluate economics.
kevin (sales_eng): blockers to call out in the one-pager:
- VPC/peering adds 2–3w and requires procurement
- If they want dedicated GPUs, need 4–6w notice + contract
- Data residency beyond region (air-gapped on-prem) is separate product stream
maria (AE): for pricing example, can we give them back-of-envelope: Hosted API: approx $0.005 / 1k prompt tokens + $0.02 / 1k completion tokens (ballpark). that gets them started vs Dedicated $X/month reserved. include both options.
aj (SE): i'll prepare an actual estimate with expected token counts and a sensitivity table (best/worst case).
jules (solutions): timeline to deliver one-pager + estimate = EOD tomorrow. i’ll ping legal for the questionnaire answers and attach the SOC2 cert.
maria (AE): perfect. customer asked for success criteria threshold — we should propose gradations: green = meets all (recommend go-live), amber = meets latency + ops but partial quality (requires further prompt tuning), red = misses latency or major hallucination issues.
tom (CS): agree. also propose rollback policy: automatic fallback to cached results for autocomplete if latency > 300ms, and fallback to smaller cheaper model for batch product desc jobs.
maria (AE): thanks team. jj to customer tomorrow 10:00 CET with one-pager. @jules @aj @kevin please drop final assets here by 09:30 CET. :thumbsup:
redwood-bot: file uploaded: soc2_v3.pdf (private)
